Hello everyone, I’m George. In the previous lecture, we outlined the characteristics and bidding process of Canadian federal government engineering projects. This session will focus on how to participate in bidding for small and medium-sized engineering projects of the Canadian federal government through the BGIS website.

The currently displayed webpage is the official BGIS website, with the URL www.bgs.merx.com. After entering this URL in the browser, the following interface will be displayed.

BGIS will list all publicly tendered small and medium-sized design and construction projects here. Currently, only project names are displayed.

BGIS will list all publicly tendered small and medium-sized design and construction projects here. Currently, only project names are displayed.

Upon entering the page, you will see the basic information of the project. This includes the Canadian Federal Government Project number (applicable to consulting and design projects), the specific project name, location, release date, deadline for inquiries, final bid submission deadline, contact information, and project overview.

This information is all the most basic content.

Under the “Notice” section on the left, “Category” primarily indicates whether the project belongs to the design or construction type, and specifies the relevant professional field involved.

Under the “Notice” section on the left, “Category” primarily indicates whether the project belongs to the design or construction type, and specifies the relevant professional field involved.

This document is actually an RFP (Request for Proposal), which is the tender for this project. Additionally, there is a smaller-scale type of project called RFQ (Request for Quotation).

The following audit content is not related to us; it’s mainly for internal audit functions. May I ask how long is left until the bidding deadline for this project?

Please note that this information is visible to all members of the public, but if you intend to participate in the bidding, you must complete the registration process. The page has a registration entry point; clicking on it will display the relevant interface, which requires filling in necessary details such as company information.

You can fill in the required information step by step and complete the payment. This service is charged annually, with credit card payments costing approximately over 200 yuan per year. Since our company is a member organization, you can log in directly.

You will notice that the interface displayed after logging in is different.

The platform has added multiple new features, including search, reports, and other membership-exclusive functions. Users can access these features by paying to become members.

The platform displays various projects—some are closed or canceled, while others remain open with active deadlines. Users can perform advanced searches based on the following criteria:
- Category (e.g., construction, electrical, etc.)
- Organization (BGIS manages not only projects for the Canadian federal government but also those for multiple state-owned enterprises)
- Province
- Date (posting date, deadline)

Next, we will briefly explain how to download tender documents from this website and prepare a bid proposal. Taking the first project as an example, click to download the relevant files.

For example, I checked the Documents, which is the complete package of the bidding documents.

I can go to the download page. After selecting “Search All,” download the file. The tender documents have now been downloaded. Assuming I have a proposal folder, I will copy the downloaded files into that folder.

The following is the complete content of the tender documents. The core document is the RP, while other appendices are components of the RP but submitted as a whole. This document is the most critical. Additionally, it includes requirements and scope descriptions for debugging, as well as specific requirements for the consulting party, which significantly impact the quotation.

This project falls under the CS category, meaning it is a design consulting project. The BGIS Requirements Document is an important file that requires careful review, as it involves multiple requirements for submitting design documents. The Project Schedule is provided by BGS, outlining their preliminary expected timeline.

The project typically involves standard clauses regarding the handling of waste and debris generated during construction, which do not require excessive attention. Appendix G is a sample ACEC agreement, serving as the contract template to be signed between BGS and the consulting firm upon winning the bid. The BGS Schedule and Cost Requirements within Appendix G specify the project schedule and cost estimates to be submitted by the winning consulting party. The Scope of Work Document in Appendix G details the project’s scope and requirements, though not all projects include this file.

The first section that requires special attention is Scope of Services and Project Description/Objective, while the remaining content mostly consists of general terms.

The second part, Terms and Conditions, can be ignored as they are all standard clauses.

The third section, Proposal Evaluation, also falls under standard content.

We need to focus on Part IV, which outlines the submission requirements for bid documents. This section details the specific requirements for the tender documents.

BGIS bidding projects typically require the tender to include two components: the price section and the technical section. The technical section usually carries more weight, while the price section is relatively straightforward.

The technical proposal section primarily includes the following content. The first part is Mandatory Requirements, where failure to meet these will disqualify subsequent eligibility, typically involving Security Clearance. The application process for security clearance will be detailed in another video.

After meeting the mandatory requirements, the main requirements of the technical proposal include:  
1. The consulting firm must provide experience and case references for similar projects.  
2. The proposed team structure for executing the project upon winning the bid.  
3. Understanding of the project.  
4. Sustainability-related content.  
5. Methodology for achieving objectives (Approach and Methodology).  
6. Reporting and issue management (Reporting and Issue Management).

Finally, the Evaluation Criteria Summary Table for the technical proposal shows that the Technical Proposal carries a 90% weight, while the price (Price Proposal) accounts for only 10%.

The Evaluation Criteria Summary Table for the technical proposal shows that the Technical Proposal carries a 90% weight, while the price (Price Proposal) accounts for only 10%.

The explanation will now proceed from Section 1.3, “Project Description and Objective.”

This section will introduce the basic information and current status of the facility.

Please note that the project scope and budget are crucial, as they typically serve as the primary basis for our design fee claims.

The scope of services for this project primarily covers all work contents of the entire project, and this is the first part.

The RFP Schedule details the timelines for question submissions and bid document submissions. This information is already covered in the initial interface and is reiterated here for emphasis.

The RFP Schedule details the timelines for question submissions and bid document submissions. This information is already covered in the initial interface and is reiterated here for emphasis.

Additionally, some projects require mandatory site visits. Failure to attend the site visit or pre-bid meeting will result in disqualification from bidding.

This is the first part of the tender document, namely Part 1 of the RFP. Next, let’s look at Part 4.

Starting from the specific requirements for tender preparation. We can see that mandatory stipulations require every staff member involved in the project to possess reliability status and security clearance.

This mainly includes the project manager.

This mainly includes the project manager.  
Lead Electrical Specialist. Additionally, the scoring criteria stipulate that the technical proposal must achieve a score of 54 points or above (out of a total 90 points) to qualify for the next round of evaluation.  
This 4.4 is talking about,  
As a consulting firm, your company has accumulated extensive experience in similar projects over the past few years.  
In this section, you need to demonstrate the company’s experience with similar past projects and explain how this experience will be reflected in the tender proposal.  
This pertains to the team structure established by the company to complete the project.  
The experience and qualifications of each core team member  
What qualifications they possess, including their career history and resume.

The experience and qualifications of each core team member, including their career history and resume.

4.6 Project Understanding, which refers to the bidder’s comprehension of the project.

Sustainable development is a relatively broad concept encompassing areas such as energy conservation and environmental protection. While the methodologies and pathways adopted to achieve the objectives may appear somewhat abstract, they must be clearly articulated. Additionally, a detailed timeline and work plan should be provided.

This section primarily elaborates on how the company should formulate the project schedule after winning the bid, clarifying the workload for each phase and the design documents that need to be completed.

The specific scoring table and bid submission requirements include detailed content for each section and page limits. The total number of pages for the bid is 16, which includes the price proposal section.

This section is relatively straightforward, mainly covering the fee proportions for each design phase and the total cost.

In addition, there is a rate schedule. Although the project adopts a fixed fee approach, consulting fees for any additional work will be calculated based on this rate schedule.

In addition, there is a rate schedule. Although the project adopts a fixed fee approach, consulting fees for any additional work will be calculated based on this rate schedule.

He calculates based on the pre-submitted rate schedule, which sets hourly rates for different positions. If the workload increases, the quotation for additional work is determined by multiplying the required man-hours for each position by their respective rates.

Additionally, the consulting firm must provide at least two meeting minutes, basic company information, and the responsible person’s signature.

The above outlines the basic situation.

Assuming we have carefully reviewed the tender documents and prepared the bid. The bid typically consists of two parts: the technical proposal and the quotation, which must strictly comply with the tenderer’s requirements.

The bid typically consists of two parts: the technical proposal and the quotation, which must strictly comply with the tenderer’s requirements.

Before the bid submission deadline, the bid must be submitted via the BGIS website. Next, I will explain the specific upload process.

Here you can see an option called “Play Speed”, just click on it.

In this step, we select “place a new bid” and then proceed with the operation.

The first step is to submit the technical proposal, the second step is to submit the price proposal, and the third step is to submit the final solution.

The first step is to submit the technical proposal, the second step is to submit the price proposal, and the third step is to submit the final solution.

How to Submit a Bid? The interface is designed to be simple and intuitive. You can upload the technical proposal and price proposal via drag-and-drop or browse function, then click “Next” until final confirmation and submission.

The above content briefly explains the entire process of selecting a project, preparing a bid, and submitting it through the BGIS website. If your company wins the bid, the BGIS Project Manager will contact you directly via phone or email. Subsequently, you will need to complete a series of documentation tasks, including providing qualification certificates and signing contracts. Once all documents are processed, the project will officially commence.
